clue.text: Dissemblings point to Conservatives

blocks.note: S, south, is a compass point
Tories are members of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: A political spin doctor directs attention towards the Conservatives.
explanation.walkthrough: Tory is the everyday British name for a Conservative politician.
explanation.definitionFit: Stories in the informal sense are lies or fibs, which are acts of dissembling.

clue.text: Girl liable to variation ?- in 33 ways

definitions.note: an allusive definition: the composer known for a waltz Beethoven varied 33 times

indicators.note: a variation is an altered version of something, so the word before it is rearranged

blocks.note: Di is a short girl's name
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A changeable girl who might behave in thirty-three different ways.
explanation.walkthrough: Beethoven's Diabelli Variations are 33 variations on a small waltz by Anton Diabelli, so the musical word 'variation' does double duty.
explanation.definitionFit: Anton Diabelli wrote the waltz theme that Beethoven famously transformed thirty-three times over in one great piano work.

clue.text: Bird liable to inspire terror in the ranks?

definitions.text: liable to inspire terror in the ranks?

blocks.note: first meaning: a dialect name for the goldfinch

blocks.clueFragment: liable to inspire terror in the ranks?
blocks.note: second meaning: a British military policeman, feared by ordinary soldiers

explanation.surface: A fearsome bird that scares the troops.
explanation.walkthrough: Royal Military Police wear red caps, hence their nickname; 'the ranks' are ordinary soldiers, who are the ones they arrest.
explanation.definitionFit: Redcap names both the goldfinch, for its crimson face, and a military policeman who frightens private soldiers.

clue.text: Meal not started before being cancelled - that's a blow

indicators.note: a thing not started lacks its beginning, so the opening letter is dropped

blocks.note: an evening meal
something cancelled has been cut

explanation.surface: Your dinner is called off before it even begins, which is a disappointment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's a blow' reads as an expression of dismay, but it is a literal blow in boxing.
explanation.definitionFit: An uppercut is a punch swung upward to the chin, a kind of blow in boxing.

clue.text: Cat seen round the church a great deal

blocks.note: O is round in shape
CE is the Church of England
a lot is a great deal

explanation.surface: A cat is often spotted prowling around the church.
explanation.definitionFit: The ocelot is a spotted wild cat of Central and South America.

clue.text: Old lover plays with model trains

indicators.note: playing with things means moving them about, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the Model T was Ford's famous car
taken as written

explanation.surface: An elderly romantic amuses himself with a model railway.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface pairs 'model trains' as a hobby; split them, and 'model' gives the letter of the Model T.
explanation.definitionFit: Tristan is the legendary medieval knight whose tragic love for Isolde is told in Arthurian romance.

clue.text: Composer who made his mark

definitions.note: a relative clause standing for a noun: one who made a mark

blocks.note: first meaning: Sir John ..., Victorian church composer
second meaning: one who leaves a stain

explanation.surface: A composer who became famous.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Made his mark' sounds like achieving fame, but read literally it is someone who leaves a stain.
explanation.definitionFit: John Stainer wrote The Crucifixion, an oratorio, and literally a stainer is a person leaving marks or discolouring things.

clue.text: Lover of food gets mince pie treatment

indicators.note: to mince is to chop finely, so the following word is cut up and reshaped

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
a cure is a medical treatment

explanation.surface: A gourmet is served mince pies.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mince pie' looks like the Christmas pastry; 'mince' is instead the instruction to chop up the word after it.
explanation.definitionFit: An epicure is a gourmet, someone devoted to refined eating and drinking.

clue.text: Quite satisfied with water?

definitions.note: a phrase describing what a well holds

blocks.note: first meaning: thoroughly pleased
second meaning: what a well contains

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the playful second reading: a well's contents are water.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means thoroughly pleased, and read literally it names the water held inside a well.

clue.text: Language barrier in American intelligence, being backward

going backward means the whole combination is read from right to left

blocks.note: a bar is a barrier
the Central Intelligence Agency

explanation.surface: US spies are hampered by not understanding a foreign tongue.
explanation.definitionFit: Arabic is the Semitic tongue spoken across North Africa and the Middle East.

clue.text: Algy sees poorly without one

indicators.note: poorly means badly or in poor shape, so the letters before it are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A toff named Algy cannot see well without his monocle.
explanation.walkthrough: Algy is the stock name of a monocled upper-class twit, so the whole clue describes the answer as well as spelling it.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyeglass is a single lens, a monocle, which a short-sighted dandy needs for clear vision.

clue.text: Penal accommodation required for current generation

blocks.note: first meaning: a prisoner's room
second meaning: a battery unit that produces electric current

explanation.surface: Prison places are needed for today's young people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current generation' suggests today's youth; it is electricity being generated.
explanation.definitionFit: A cell is a prisoner's room, and also a single unit of a battery producing electricity.

clue.text: Suspect article in pawn may lead to speedy apprehension

definitions.note: a descriptive phrase for the answer rather than a synonym

one thing in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: to pop something is British slang for pawning it
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A stolen item turning up at the pawnbroker's could get the thief arrested quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speedy apprehension' sounds like a quick arrest, but it is the arrest of speeding drivers.
explanation.definitionFit: A speed trap set by officers on the road catches motorists who drive too fast.

clue.text: Medical study of unbeliever in Hades  ...

indicators.note: one thing in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: Dis is the Roman god of the underworld, and his realm
an agnostic does not commit to belief in God

explanation.surface: Research into a doubter's condition in the underworld.
explanation.walkthrough: Dis is the classical underworld, the same place as Hades; the three dots link to 19 across, which also treats Hades.
explanation.definitionFit: Diagnostics is the branch of medicine concerned with identifying diseases from symptoms.

clue.text: "Morning" from Grieg: ten pieces

definitions.note: the quoted word is said as a salutation

indicators.note: broken into pieces means the letters are smashed and reassembled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Morning, from Grieg's Peer Gynt music, is one of ten pieces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Morning' is the famous Grieg movement, but here it is what one says on meeting someone.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying "Morning!" is a salutation offered on meeting someone early in the day.

clue.text: Added financial commitments make officer peevish

blocks.note: abbreviation for captain
IOUs are written promises to repay debts

explanation.surface: Mounting debts put an officer in a bad mood.
explanation.definitionFit: Captious describes someone fault-finding and quick to raise petty objections, so irritable and carping.

clue.text: Dead in bed - and none too soon!

indicators.note: one thing in another means it is placed inside it

blocks.note: taken as written
the late someone is someone who has died

explanation.surface: Someone dies in bed, and some think it was about time.
explanation.definitionFit: Belated means arriving after the expected time, so certainly not early.

clue.text: State trial is corrupt and biased

indicators.note: corrupt means spoiled or altered from its true form, so the word is rearranged

blocks.note: PA is the postal abbreviation for Pennsylvania
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A government trial has been rigged and is unfair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'State trial' reads as one prosecution; split it, and 'State' is an American state.
explanation.definitionFit: Partial means favouring one side, prejudiced rather than impartial.

clue.text: ... a true description of Hades?

blocks.note: surface reading: an accurate account of the underworld
setter's reading: Hades is the middle place of those who have died, and the middle letter of the word itself is D

explanation.surface: An honest account of what the underworld is like.
explanation.walkthrough: The phrase means exactly in the middle; Hades is where the dead are gathered, and the dots continue from 14 across.
explanation.definitionFit: Hades houses departed souls, so it is literally the hub of the departed, while the idiom means precisely central.

clue.text: Send down for speedo tampering

indicators.note: tampering means interfering with something so its parts no longer stay as they were

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A motorist is jailed for fiddling with the speedometer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Send down' suggests a prison sentence; here it means remove from office. A speedo is the speedometer.
explanation.definitionFit: To depose a ruler is to remove them from power, bringing them down from the throne.

clue.text: Anyway, no use catching first train from here

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
opening letter of the word

explanation.surface: It is pointless trying to catch the first train from this station anyway.
explanation.walkthrough: EUSTON is a major London railway terminus, which explains 'from here'.
explanation.definitionFit: London's Euston terminus is where intercity trains to the north-west depart, so a journey starts there.

clue.text: Roger is taken in by a girl - the fool!

explanation.walkthrough: PRAT is British slang for an idiot.
explanation.definitionFit: Prat is British slang for a stupid or incompetent person, an idiot.

clue.text: Russian member of religious order Puritans dissolved  ...

explanation.walkthrough: The dots run on to 24 across, also about religion.

clue.text: Worker with vegetables?

explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes a farm labourer, while 'with' places the worker beside the vegetables.
explanation.definitionFit: A peasant is a small farmer or rural labourer who grows crops on the land.

clue.text: Democratic East End neighbourhood goes round the bend

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it

blocks.note: Poplar is a district in London's East End
a U-bend is shaped like the letter

explanation.surface: A working-class area of London is driven mad.
